title: Audit streaming examples across Python/TS/Go + docs; produce parity matrix + canonical pattern proposal
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Complete a cross-repo audit of streaming examples and docs (Python SDK, TypeScript SDK, Go SDK, redwood-docs, redwood-examples/quickstarts) and identify mismatches that cause copy/paste failures or inconsistent mental models.
- Deliverables for Week 1:
  1) Parity matrix (what exists today, what’s broken/outdated, what differs).
  2) Proposed canonical pattern for streaming consumption + tool calling + structured output references (to be codified in Confluence standards + ADR).

Context
Support + Solutions are seeing repeated confusion around:
- Event naming differences across languages (e.g., “delta” vs “chunk”; mixing message-assembly and logging in the same loop).
- Tool-call arguments mid-stream appearing truncated; examples incorrectly attempting to parse tool args before the stream finalizes.
- Structured output snippets that parse JSON incrementally during streaming without guardrails.

In-scope sources
- SDK READMEs and docs: redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-go
- Docs pages: streaming guide, tool calling guide, structured output guide
- Runnable examples/quickstarts: redwood-examples, redwood-quickstarts

Audit method
1) Inventory existing snippets and categorize by scenario:
   - Basic streaming (assistant text)
   - Streaming + tool calling (single tool)
   - Streaming + tool calling (parallel tools)
   - Tool-result loop (assistant -> tool call -> tool result -> assistant)
   - Structured output (non-streaming) with JSON schema + validation
   - Structured output (streaming) w/ caveats
2) Compile mismatches into a parity matrix with columns:
   - Location (repo/path), language, model string used, SDK version assumption
   - Event types shown, assembly logic, error handling, disconnect/retry guidance
   - Tool calling shape, tool result message shape, validation/typing strategy
   - Copy/paste status (passes, fails, flaky), repro notes
3) Propose canonical pattern:
   - “Minimum footgun” streaming loop across languages
   - Clear do/don’t guidance (especially: don’t parse tool args until tool_call is finalized)

Deliverables
- Parity matrix (Drive) with top-priority fixes flagged P0/P1.
- Summary write-up + canonical pattern proposal shared in DevEx/Docs sync.
- Follow-up tickets created/linked for each repo change (Python/TS/Go/docs/examples).

Notes / constraints
- Do not propose protocol-level changes (examples/SDK ergonomics only).
- Keep examples compatible with released SDKs; if behavior differs by version, note it explicitly and pick a single recommended minimum version for docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parity matrix completed and shared (link in ticket) with at least: Python/TS/Go SDK examples, docs streaming page(s), and one runnable example per language.
- List of mismatches grouped by: (a) streaming event handling, (b) tool calling, (c) structured output.
- Canonical streaming + tool calling pattern proposal written (pseudocode + example conventions) and reviewed asynchronously by SDK + Docs leads.
- Concrete follow-up issues created/linked for P0/P1 fixes (SDK + docs + examples).
audit_findings:
High-level findings (Week 1)

1) Streaming event model inconsistencies
- Python examples tended to show “print(chunk)” style loops without clear final message assembly; TS showed partial assembly but different naming; Go had a simpler consumer loop but lacked explicit finalization guidance.
- Docs streaming guide mixed event terminology (delta/chunk/message) and did not make it explicit which events are stable vs “SDK convenience wrappers”.
- Several snippets logged partial deltas but never demonstrated reconstructing the final assistant message deterministically (hard to adapt for tool args and structured outputs).

2) Tool calling mismatches and common footguns
- Two snippet families exist internally:
  (a) Treating tool args as a single JSON blob available immediately.
  (b) Treating tool args as a streamed string that must be buffered until final tool_call event.
  Some docs implicitly assumed (a), while support tickets and real traces behave like (b) for some models and/or streaming modes.
- At least one TS snippet used a tool-result message shape that didn’t match the SDK’s current types (caused SUP-18452 style errors).
- Examples generally did not demonstrate parallel tool calls, but docs claimed parallel capability without a working copy/paste sample.

3) Structured output guidance gaps
- Multiple examples parsed JSON during streaming without a “wait for completion then validate” step, causing JSON parse errors and confusing retries.
- Docs did not clearly state that structured output guarantees are model-dependent; language suggested “JSON mode” behavior universally.

4) Copy/paste failures observed during audit
- TS: tool calling example type mismatch + result shape mismatch in at least one location (compile-time failure).
- Go: streaming example didn’t show retry/disconnect branch; users copy it and end up with silent partial outputs.
- Docs code tabs: language tabs were out of sync; Python showed older snippet pattern vs TS/Go.

P0 recommendations
- Unify on one canonical streaming loop per language: explicit event switching, buffer deltas, finalize on terminal event, and include error/disconnect handling.
- For tool calls: always buffer tool_call.arguments deltas; only JSON-parse at “tool_call.completed” (or equivalent terminal signal in SDK).
- For structured output: validate at end (JSON schema), with retry fallback; include explicit warning about incremental JSON parsing.
proposed_canonical_pattern:
Canonical pattern proposal (to be codified in Confluence + used across docs/SDK READMEs)

Principles
- One mental model across languages: stream emits typed events; you handle them in a switch; you buffer partial deltas; you assemble a final assistant message deterministically.
- Treat tool calls as first-class messages: assistant may request tool(s); client runs tools; client returns tool results; assistant continues.
- Structured output is validated output: parse + validate after the message completes; streaming is for UX, not for partial parsing.

Event conventions to show in examples
- response.started: initialize buffers + request_id
- response.output_text.delta: append assistant text delta to a text buffer (for printing) and/or message buffer
- response.tool_call.delta: append tool arguments delta to a per-tool-call buffer (string buffer)
- response.tool_call.completed: parse arguments JSON once; validate against tool schema; enqueue tool execution
- response.error: surface error; include retry guidance (idempotency note)
- response.completed: finalize; print/log final assistant message + tool call transcript summary

Example-level guidance (do/don’t)
DO
- Keep a single assembly path that yields a final message object + transcript.
- Buffer tool args during streaming; JSON.parse only after completion.
- Demonstrate tool result message shape explicitly (tool name, call_id, content/result).
- Include minimal retry snippet for disconnect/timeout with a warning about duplicate tool execution.

DON’T
- Don’t show parsing tool arguments in the delta handler.
- Don’t imply structured output guarantees across all models without a support matrix callout.
- Don’t mix multiple competing event names in docs (pick the canonical ones).
outcome: Audit completed; parity matrix delivered; canonical pattern proposal shared and used to drive follow-up PRs/tickets across SDKs and docs.
